effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the Bedrock Genesis Block specification, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core, logos-blockchain-ledger, logos-blockchain-tools or logos-blockchain-config that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

Where the specification lives in the code:
- core/src/block/genesis.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the genesis block type, its header fields and the rules that make a block a genesis block. core/src/mantle/transactions/genesis_tx.rs and src/mantle/traits/genesis.rs: the genesis transaction (initial note distribution, initial inscriptions) and its validation. core/src/mantle/fixtures/genesis.rs: test genesis builders.
- ledger/src/lib.rs and src/cryptarchia/mod.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): how the ledger is initialised from the genesis block, the initial epoch state (nonce, stake snapshot, total stake), and what of the genesis is checked at startup.
- tools/blockchain-tools/src/genesis/ (mod.rs, distribution.rs, inscription.rs) and src/bin/genesis.rs (package `logos-blockchain-tools`): the genesis generator operators run; its output format is what nodes consume. tools/config/src/consensus.rs (package `logos-blockchain-config`): how a generated deployment config references the genesis.
- Adjacent, outside the unit: the Mantle specification (transaction and operation formats the genesis transaction reuses, audited by another brief), nodes/node/binary/src/config/ (how the node loads the genesis file).

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
